issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the solution implementation defines acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This discrepancy can confuse students about the correct method signature they must implement and may cause mismatches with tests or expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the signature across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to require acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the unused supplier parameter), or modify the solution and any tests to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Ensure the template (SealSaloon to be created by students) and tests use the same signature.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — signature shown as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The solution implementation defines acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) and omits the supplier name parameter. This mismatch between the described API and the provided implementation can confuse students about the required method signature and parameter semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the solution (and template) to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — keeping supplierName as a (possibly unused) parameter — or update the problem statement and UML to require only (String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Prefer updating the code to match the documented UML if the supplier name is intended to be part of the API.
